title: Gen Z and millennials are sequencing ambition around stability, sustainable work, purpose and AI readiness rather than rejecting advancement
source_unit: Deloitte Global 2026 Gen Z and Millennial Survey, Progress on Their Own Terms
geography: 44 countries; global survey of Gen Z and millennial adults with supplementary qualitative insights from business leaders

observations.period: 2026 survey; more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries

denominator.unit: more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents; exact total reported by Deloitte as more than 22,500

cost_of_living_priority.value: Cost of living remains the top concern for Gen Zs and millennials for the fifth consecutive year

paycheck_to_paycheck.value: Nearly half report living paycheck to paycheck

housing_career_link.value: Housing availability or affordability directly affects where 69% of Gen Zs and 64% of millennials can work and their career decisions

life_decision_delay.value: 55% of Gen Zs and 52% of millennials say finances are delaying major decisions such as marriage, family, business or further education

observations.method: Deloitte global survey of Gen Z and millennial adults across 44 countries, supplemented by qualitative interviews with business leaders.
observations.uncertainty: The public report is a Deloitte-sponsored cross-sectional survey and does not establish causal effects of housing or inflation on decisions; reported percentages may reflect country-composition and self-report differences.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z respondents born 1995–2007 and millennial respondents born 1983–1994, compared across 44 countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Financial caution may coexist with optimism and strategic planning; delayed milestones do not necessarily imply disengagement or lower long-run aspiration.

denominator.unit: more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries

rapid_promotion_preference.value: 25% of Gen Zs and 21% of millennials prefer rapid promotions and title changes

leadership_primary_goal.value: Only 6% of Gen Zs and millennials identify achieving a leadership position as their primary career goal

leadership_interest.value: 76% of Gen Zs and 67% of millennials remain interested in pursuing senior or executive leadership roles over their careers

organizational_change_agency.value: 69% believe they have power to drive change within their organization

observations.method: Cross-sectional survey questions on ideal career path, leadership interest, barriers and perceived organizational agency.
observations.uncertainty: Career preferences and perceived agency are not observed promotion, retention or performance outcomes; the survey cannot identify whether organizational conditions later change.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z and millennial employees or workers across the 44-country sample.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower preference for rapid promotion can reflect a shift toward sustainable progression and skill accumulation, not reduced ambition; high long-run leadership interest supports that reading.

observations.period: 2026 survey; AI use and organizational readiness

denominator.unit: more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries

work_ai_use.value: 74% of both Gen Zs and millennials report using AI to some extent in day-to-day work

ai_growth_support.value: 79% use AI to identify learning and development opportunities; 72% of Gen Zs and 69% of millennials seek career advice with it

ai_stress_support.value: 67% of Gen Zs and 65% of millennials use AI to cope with work-related stress

organizational_readiness.value: Around one-third do not believe employers sufficiently train employees on AI, and around 30% say employers are not prepared for AI-driven changes

observations.method: Survey of self-reported workplace AI use, use cases, training and employer readiness, with year-over-year comparisons in the report.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported AI use does not measure task quality, productivity, displacement, verification or employer implementation; the report is not a workplace field experiment.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z and millennial workers, with separate generational percentages where reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI use can represent experimentation or low-stakes assistance rather than deep adoption; the readiness gap may reflect changing expectations as much as actual organizational failure.

observations.period: 2026 survey; well-being, digital fatigue and purpose

denominator.unit: more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries

mental_health_good.value: 63% of Gen Zs and 66% of millennials rate their mental health as good or extremely good, up from 52% and 58% respectively in 2025

frequent_stress.value: Roughly one-third report feeling anxious or stressed most or all of the time

digital_fatigue.value: 58% of Gen Zs and 54% of millennials report digital fatigue from constant alerts and navigating multiple tools and platforms

purpose_at_work.value: 96% of Gen Zs and 97% of millennials say having a sense of purpose at work is important to job satisfaction

observations.method: Repeated annual survey measures combined with questions on work stress, digital fatigue, purpose and workplace support.
observations.uncertainty: Mental-health and fatigue measures are self-assessments and should not be read as clinical prevalence; year-over-year changes may reflect sample, wording or composition effects.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z and millennial workers across 44 countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved self-rated mental health can coexist with persistent stress because people may adapt expectations, support systems or coping practices without removing structural pressure.

related_sources.claim: Official Deloitte landing page with report framing, headline findings and 44-country scope.
Deloitte press-release context for the 15th anniversary edition and qualitative business-leader component.

boundary: This record adds a global work-and-life sequencing layer: financial and housing constraints are changing the timing and conditions of ambition, while AI adoption is outpacing organizational readiness and purpose remains central to job satisfaction. It is a Deloitte-sponsored cross-sectional survey with qualitative leader insight, not a representative longitudinal labor panel, causal evaluation, clinical assessment, employer performance audit or proof of actual AI productivity or displacement.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Deloitte landing page and 53-page 2026 PDF were retrieved and reviewed for sample scope, financial pressure, housing, milestone timing, career progression, leadership, AI use/readiness, mental health, digital fatigue and purpose findings; the PDF was hashed.
